title: Max Consecutive Ones II
summary: For a binary array, determine the longest sequence of consecutive 1's that can be achieved by flipping at most one 0.
statement: For a binary array, determine the longest sequence of consecutive 1's that can be achieved by flipping at most one 0.
constraints: Flip at most one zero, then return the longest consecutive run of ones. An all-one array needs no flip.
The follow-up asks for constant extra memory even when values arrive as a stream; retaining the full prefix is unnecessary.
hints: Only the runs immediately beside one chosen zero can be joined.
Keep the current run and the run before the most recent zero, including that zero as one flipped position.
On a one, extend current. On a zero, set before_zero=current+1 and reset current. Update best with before_zero+current.
A second zero replaces the previous bridge. Three counters suffice, and an all-one stream never adds a nonexistent flipped position.
editorial: The two adjacent runs identify the longest valid suffix crossing the most recent zero. Older zeros cannot participate in that suffix, so their state can be discarded. This supports a one-pass iterator with constant extra memory. The independent oracle flips each possible zero in a copy and measures literal one-runs.

tests.explanation: Flip the first zero to connect the neighboring runs into four ones. Flipping the final zero gives only three.
One flip cannot bridge two adjacent zeros. The longest possible run is 3, not the total number of ones plus one.
